newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mahathir urges Japan firms to join multimedia hub.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir urges Japan firms to join multimedia hub.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad urged Japanese companies on Monday to join his nation's multimedia project, touting the plan as a rare investment opportunity unseen in other developed nations.
"Many of the wealthier developed countries are locked into obsolete industrial systems and legislative frameworks," Mahathir told a group of Japanese business leaders.
"We hope this (project) will accelerate our (nation's) economic development and create exciting opportunities that our international partners cannot pursue elsewhere," he said.

Mahathir, on a four-day trip to Japan to promote his nation's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) project, met Japanese business executives on Monday after a week-long roadshow in California last week to persuade top information technology companies to invest in the project.
Mahathir said the recently concluded U.S. leg of his tour, where he met media and computer technology business leaders of firms such as Microsoft Corp and Sony Corp was "overwhelmingly positive."

Some 30 companies in the United States expressed the wish to participate in the project, although none has specified the area of interest or the amount of investment, Mahathir told a news conference after his presentation.
Asked about the interest in Japan, Mahathir said, "So far, Japanese companies seem to show very keen interest...they have expressed strong support for the project."
The 15 km-by-50 km (nine mile-by-25 mile) corridor will initially be driven by three mega-projects that will be major consumers of multimedia products and services.
One is the new capital of Putrajaya, designed to be an "intelligent city" with a paperless administration.
The others are a new airport and the Kuala Lumpur City Centre, a massive office project featuring the Petronas Twin Towers, the world's tallest buildings at 452 metres (1,482 feet).
"The Information Age has created for the first time in history a chance which will enable countries and companies to mutually enrich each other," Mahathir said.
"There is a tremendous opportunity for countries and companies that have courage to embrace these changes," he said.
